## Window search

The original search script and cached runs are not in this repository. The block below records its documented settings; it is **not executable search code**.

<details class="analysis-code" open>
<summary>Show recorded search settings</summary>

```r
# Documented settings, transcribed from the analysis record.
# No sliding-window search is called in this block.
search_settings <- list(
  response = "annual median laying date",
  reference_date = "7 May",
  candidate_range_weeks = c(17, 0),
  resolution = "complete calendar-week bins",
  temperature_summary = "arithmetic mean",
  response_model = "linear temperature effect; intercept-only baseline",
  randomised_full_searches = 500,
  training_years = c(1980, 2002),
  held_out_years = c(2003, 2025),
  excluded_field_year = 2020
)
search_settings
```

</details>

## Operational window for the reproductive models

The reproductive analyses used **26 March–7 May**, a fixed 43-day interval. This differs from the complete-week search window.

<details class="analysis-code">
<summary>Show original code: 00_check_public_inputs.R</summary>

{{< include _includes/00_check_public_inputs.qmd >}}

</details>

| 1980 | 3.3535 | 2.3364 | 43 | 1980-03-26 | 1980-05-07 |
| 1981 | 3.3372 | 1.8033 | 43 | 1981-03-26 | 1981-05-07 |
| 1982 | 3.7488 | 1.5051 | 43 | 1982-03-26 | 1982-05-07 |

## Main conclusions

- Warmer conditions in the selected weekly period were associated with earlier laying; the association remained in held-out years.
- Reproductive models use the fixed 43-day exposure, not the complete-week search dates.
- This validates a phenology association, not reproductive outcomes; window-selection uncertainty was not propagated into those models.
